title: review: S3 v4: orchestrator/critical_path.py — deterministic critical-path ranking of ready tasks (recursive downstream chain, blocked descendants, cold-start durations) wired as the daemon's wave order (spec review T-0540 folded in)
spec:
Goal T-0503, brief .orchestrator/adaptive-parallelism-program.md section P4 (prioritize tasks that determine goal completion time; design and test a ranking function, do not implement the sketch blindly) and P5 (cold start simple and deterministic, no false precision). Base goal/T-0503 with S2 v4 (T-0534) merged: daemon._wave_order(candidate_ids, tasks) identity hook; waves.jsonl row has an empty "priority"; the tasks dict covers candidates, running and their transitive depends_on ancestry. Work only in your worktree, commit only on your own branch with the task id in the message, run the full .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh before reporting; report sha and failures only. Tests are unittest.TestCase methods (the gate runs unittest discover).
Facts: tasks are dicts with id, parent, depends_on, status, merged_into, complexity, constraints; bus.dependents(tid) (bus.py:153-155) returns every task, any status, whose depends_on names tid; scorecard._band (scorecard.py:56) maps complexity to bands 1-3, 4-6, 7-10. A dependent is "unresolved" unless it is merged (merged_into set) or failed; queued, held (budget retries) and running dependents all count.
1. New orchestrator/critical_path.py, pure: est_duration_s(task, durations=None) = durations[task id] if present, else durations[band] if present, else COLD_START_S = {"1-3": 600, "4-6": 1200, "7-10": 2400} by complexity band. critical_path_s(t) = est_duration_s(t) + max(critical_path_s(child) for child in unresolved direct dependents of t within tasks, default 0), memoised, with a visiting set so a back edge is ignored and never recursed (no hang). explain(task_id, tasks, durations=None) -> {"downstream_depth": longest chain of unresolved transitive dependents (edges), "blocked_descendants": number of distinct unresolved transitive dependents, "est_duration_s", "critical_path_s", "priority": critical_path_s}. rank(ready_ids, tasks, durations=None) -> ids sorted by priority desc, then blocked_descendants desc, then id asc; deterministic; ids not in tasks keep their relative order at the end.
2. daemon: _wave_order(candidate_ids, tasks) returns critical_path.rank(candidate_ids, tasks); the waves.jsonl row's "priority" becomes {id: explain(...)} for every candidate. Extend the tasks dict built in dispatch with the transitive dependents of every candidate via bus.dependents, keeping execute tasks that are unresolved (not merged, not failed) whatever their status; state this in a comment. In shadow mode the order is only logged (baseline_order stays first-come); in active mode the wave is dispatched in this order.
3. README Pipeline paragraph: one sentence on the ranking and its cold-start durations.
4. Tests: tests/test_critical_path.py::test_rank_prefers_longer_downstream_chain, ::test_rank_tie_breaks_on_blocked_descendants_then_id, ::test_explain_cold_start_durations_by_band, ::test_rank_ignores_merged_and_failed_descendants, ::test_rank_handles_cycles, ::test_durations_override_cold_start, ::test_critical_path_sums_along_the_whole_chain (A -> B -> C with durations 1, 10, 100: critical_path_s(A) = 111, not 11); tests/test_daemon.py::test_wave_row_carries_priority_order (two ready candidates, one with a budget-held dependent: the wave order puts it first and the row's priority explains both). Existing tests stay green.
acceptance: tests/test_critical_path.py::test_rank_prefers_longer_downstream_chain, tests/test_critical_path.py::test_rank_tie_breaks_on_blocked_descendants_then_id, tests/test_critical_path.py::test_rank_ignores_merged_and_failed_descendants, tests/test_critical_path.py::test_rank_handles_cycles and tests/test_critical_path.py::test_critical_path_sums_along_the_whole_chain pass: rank orders a task that unblocks a longer or heavier chain first, breaks ties by blocked descendants then id, ignores merged and failed descendants, terminates on cycles, and critical_path_s accumulates along the whole chain

tests/test_critical_path.py::test_explain_cold_start_durations_by_band and tests/test_critical_path.py::test_durations_override_cold_start pass: explain reports downstream_depth, blocked_descendants, est_duration_s (600/1200/2400 s by band unless durations override) and critical_path_s

tests/test_daemon.py::test_wave_row_carries_priority_order passes: the waves.jsonl row carries priority explanations for all candidates, held dependents count, the wave order follows rank, and shadow mode still dispatches first-come
full .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 and the suite gains eight tests
